methodology: Every entry's evidence field traces to something actually built and, where possible, actually tested - not a claim restated from the original project plan. A review comparing the original plan against verified reality found several plan items were aspirational or simply not built; those are excluded here rather than included with a hedge. status values: implemented | partial | not_applicable.

controls.name: Prompt Injection
controls.evidence: Input guardrail (guardrails.py) blocks requests matching seven documented regex patterns before any request reaches the model - confirmed via latency_ms: 0 on every blocked request, proving the model was never called. Covered by a 10-case automated regression suite (tests/test_assistant_guardrails.py) verifying all seven adversarial patterns and three clean-question false-positive checks.

controls.name: Insecure Output Handling
controls.evidence: Output guardrail (redact_output in guardrails.py) scans every model response for OpenAI keys, AWS access keys, bearer tokens, and private key blocks before it reaches the client, replacing matches with a labeled placeholder.

controls.name: Model Denial of Service
controls.evidence: The AI assistant endpoint is covered by the general Redis rate limit tier (60/min), not a dedicated, tighter AI-specific tier - confirmed directly against rate_limit.py. Token counts are recorded on every request (ai_requests.input_tokens/ output_tokens) but no enforced per-user token budget exists yet.

controls.name: Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
controls.evidence: SBOM generation, pip-audit, and Trivy container scanning in CI. Six real CVEs fixed with functional verification (not just a green build), three documented as evidence-based accepted risk with expiry dates in .trivyignore, one genuinely deferred with documented root-cause analysis.

controls.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
controls.evidence: RAG retrieval applies a server-side document-ID allowlist at query time via a Chroma metadata filter, never as a post-hoc filter on already-returned results. Verified with an automated canary/honeytoken script (verify_rag_canary.py) that plants a unique secret through the real upload pipeline and confirms it is invisible to a different real user while still retrievable by its owner - not just a manual one-time check.

controls.name: Overreliance
controls.evidence: Every AI response carries a real disclaimer field (confirmed in live API responses). Surfacing this in the governance dashboard itself is the feature this phase is actively building.

frameworks.name: MITRE ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems)

controls.name: LLM Prompt Injection
controls.evidence: Same as OWASP LLM01 above - input guardrail plus automated regression suite.

controls.name: LLM Data Leakage
controls.evidence: Same as OWASP LLM06 above - retrieval-time permission filter, verified by the canary script.

controls.name: Brute Force (Credential Access)
controls.evidence: Account lockout after a configured failed-attempt threshold, plus IP-based rate limiting on the login endpoint. Both mechanisms were directly debugged and fixed this session - they initially shared an identical threshold, causing rate limiting to always intercept the request meant to trigger lockout, making the more specific 423 response unreachable.

controls.name: Account Manipulation (Persistence)
controls.evidence: Every role change is written to the append-only audit_log table with actor and timestamp.

controls.name: Impair Defenses (Defense Evasion)
controls.evidence: audit_log is INSERT-only at the database grant level - the application's own DB role cannot UPDATE or DELETE it.

controls.name: Broken Object Level Authorization
controls.evidence: Document-level permission checks on every access, verified with 404-not-403 tests confirming existence isn't leaked to unauthorized users.

controls.name: Broken Authentication
controls.evidence: JWT with short-lived access tokens, opaque rotated refresh tokens, Argon2id password hashing, account lockout.

controls.name: Broken Function Level Authorization
controls.evidence: require_roles() dependency, applied for the first time this phase to the governance endpoints. Verified both branches directly against a real account: a viewer-role token receives an actual 403 with the exact expected message, and the same account promoted to security_engineer receives 200 with real data.

controls.name: Broken Access Control
controls.evidence: RBAC plus object-level permission checks throughout - same evidence as API1/API5 above.

controls.name: Injection
controls.evidence: Parameterized queries via SQLAlchemy throughout; Semgrep SAST gate in CI catches string-built-query patterns before merge.

controls.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
controls.evidence: Same as LLM05 above - pip-audit, Trivy, and the full CVE remediation history.

controls.name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
controls.evidence: audit_log table plus Prometheus scraping the backend, confirmed via direct target-health check (health: up) during Phase 7 testing.

controls.name: Map
controls.evidence: Threat Modeling Module applied to the platform's own RAG cross-tenant isolation - the platform reviewing itself with the same rigor it applies to submitted code.

controls.name: Manage
controls.evidence: AI-specific incident response runbook covering seven real scenarios (prompt injection, guardrail bypass, RAG leakage, malware, credential exposure, provider outage, dependency CVEs), each tied to a real endpoint, script, or table rather than generic guidance.

controls.name: Audit and Accountability
controls.evidence: audit_log table, INSERT-only grant, now readable via the governance dashboard's own audit-log endpoint.

controls.name: System and Information Integrity
controls.evidence: ClamAV malware scanning (Phase 2), SAST/dependency/container scanning in CI (Phase 7).

controls.name: Risk Assessment
controls.evidence: Threat Modeling Module plus CI SAST/DAST gates providing continuous, not point-in-time, risk assessment.

frameworks.name: EU AI Act (good-faith functional alignment, not a compliance certification)

controls.name: Transparency
controls.evidence: Every AI response carries a real disclaimer field, confirmed present in live API responses, not just documented as a plan.

controls.name: Human Oversight
controls.evidence: No auto-remediation exists anywhere in the platform - finding status changes require an explicit human action via PATCH /governance/findings/{id}/status, and every such change is itself audit-logged with before/after values.
